input.reasoning_summary: All three challenges were refuted by the evidence. H1: Stock-based compensation in R&D increased by $500 million (from $832M to $1,332M per E10), which is only about 27% of the total $1.87B R&D increase. E2 explicitly states the increase was "primarily due to increases in costs related to AI and other programs" with stock-based compensation mentioned separately as an additional factor. H2: Restructuring charges totaled $390 million in 2025 (E14), which is significantly less than the $1.87B R&D increase driven by AI. H3: The filing consistently states AI was a primary driver, using the phrase "primarily due to increases in costs related to AI and other programs" (E2, E4), indicating AI was the leading factor. The R&D increase of $1.87B far exceeds the SG&A increase of $684M, confirming that AI-related R&D was indeed the primary driver of operating expense increases in 2025. The initial verdict remains SUPPORTED.
